Man oh man does this game blow. So many stupid design choices just remove all ability to have fun in the game.

the core game does get repetitive but still entertaining. the problem for me is the fact that the devs seem to encourage a style of play that is just not very immersive and boils down to "go fast, break the game." maybe they'll start to change that with patches in the future, but as of now and the recent patch, they seem to be more concerned with making the game harder for regular non-speed-run players to try and pad out play time (or maybe sell you something in the future). the levels feel a bit lazy and a lot of locations are just reused over and over. the skins also feel like a phoned in attempt to leave space for maybe future microtransactions or dlc and i don't find myself really wanting to go out of my way to unlock them. there are also a lot of just small user experience things that are missing or are just frustrating to deal with (no meaningful scoreboard, no leave game with party, no weapon attachment management system, can't do anything about afk players etc). the guns and animations feel pretty solid but the UI feels unfinished and rushed. There are a lot of weird network/server issues too where zombies just seem to freeze for a sec and suddenly teleport even when you're latency is sub 50. I don't know, the game just doesn't give off a very strong sense of quality no matter how I look at it.

TLDR: can be entertaining but un-fun meta. devs have questionable future plans IMO. get it on sale and not full price

Back 4 Blood is a first-person co-op shooter in the likes of Left 4 Dead. It is made by the devs of L4D.
 
[h1]Campaign[/h1]
The campaign consists of 4 acts, each with several levels. In total, there are over 30 levels with more to come. The level design is on par with Left 4 Dead's IMO. It's nice to jump into a session for a bit and just have fun. Different difficulty settings (pretty hard IMO) paired with "runs" add a lot to the replayability of the game. Unlike Left 4 Dead each run is different… to some extend. It's not like a whole different campaign but since you will get event cards at every level, it will be a bit different every time (some levels will have a boss then, fog, special zombies, etc.). All in all, the campaign is very well made.
 
[h1]Swarm Mode[/h1]
Swarm mode is a 4v4 player mode. 4 cleaners vs 4 special zombies. Each round the teams changes their site and who survives the longest gets a point. It's the best of three and the team who wins 2 rounds wins the match. It's a short and pretty fun mode. The only thing I'm missing is something like a rank. I don't want it to get too competitive but I had several matches where you immediately notice after the first 30 seconds which team is better (by a lot). If you have 2 of those matches one after another the fun is gone and you don't want to play anymore. You can't even leave the match because you will immediately get locked out of matchmaking for 5 minutes (leaving more often results in longer times). I get why they added this but since there is no skill-based matchmaking (as far as I notice), it just sucks.
 
[h1]Cards[/h1]
This is something completely new compared to leaving 4 dead. There are dozens of cards in the game. For every run, you start or Swarm matches you play, you need to select a deck of up to 15 cards. Each round/level you draw one of five new cards, adding buffs to the game (15 more health, a knife, 10% faster reload times, etc.). Since you can build your own deck, you can decide how you want to play. Be a tank, med, supporter, specialize in melee or guns, etc. There are endless possibilities through a game like this that will always have a meta.
 
[h1]Progression[/h1]
This is a tricky one. I like progression in games but in Back 4 Blood it takes waaaay too long to unlock everything. For every match played (let it be campaign or swarm mode) you get supplies. With supplies, you can unlock the next "level" in a line of 8 levels. You have three of them activated at once (Supply lines) and need to completely unlock one (8 items/cards) to get a new one. You can unlock cards and cosmetics.
 
[h1]The Good[/h1][list]
[*]The gameplay. The gunplay is amazing and just addictive. Shooting zombies is just so much fun even for someone (me) who isn't really into shooters that much. They nailed it gameplay-wise 100%!
[*]The campaign. It's not as good as L4D's (Nostalgia probably) but still good enough and way better in games that came out in the meantime and wanted to fill the void (Earthfall to name one).
[*]Cards. They spice the game up just right. It's a welcome addition to the genre and adds a lot of replay value. I like it very much. Thanks to that, runs can be different enough to have high replayability.
[*]Swarm Mode. I like it way more than the zombie mode in L4D (4v4, playing a full campaign) because it is way shorter. Just wanna play 30 minutes? Go ahead. You will have enough time to probably play two full matches.
[*]Difficulty. Even on easy the game is pretty hard playing with randoms sometimes. You won't have an easy time easier way because, with a pre-made team, you can easily have a hard time on the highest difficulty setting.
[*]Progression. While I don't think it's perfect in the slightest, I very much appreciate having any form of progression at all.[/list]

[h1]The Bad[/h1][list]
[*]There is no endless mode. One of the supposedly most fun and obvious modes in horde games isn't even in Back 4 Blood. The only thing I can think of is them wanting you to spend additional cash in the future for this "new feature".
[*]The progression is too slow. You will need several dozens of hours to unlock everything the game has to offer as of now. You get way too few points/supplies/whatever it is called in English per match. I know this is how modern gaming works but it still sucks.
[*]More variety when it comes to objectives in the campaign. Even though there are already a handful of different objectives in the game (deploying bombs, defending a house, getting suitcases on a truck, shooting nests, etc.) you will have the same (shooting nests) in like 60% of levels.
[*]Matchmaking in swarm. There isn't really a matchmaking system in place. I mean, technically there is but there are no ranks or anything so you'll get into games with whoever searches for a game, too. This can result in you facing teams with over 200 hours of playtime while your team consists of newbies who don't even know the four standard decks.
[*]Endless crashes, freezes and Bugs. It happened so many times, that the game randomly stopped working. This also happened to a few friends of mine when we wanted to play together.
[*]I had several occasions when I searched for a game (Swarm mode), found one, got into one (this takes 1-2 minutes already) just to get kicked out because too many players left or whatever and needed to search manually again. All of this can take 2-3 minutes just so you need to restart the search again (why not search automatically?). This is one of the MANY QOL features missing in this full-priced triple-A game, where the devs brag about having 10+ years of experience in game development.
[*]To name a few: Can't vote to kick players, can't remove weapon attachments at all (they want to add a CARD for that lmao), no single-player progression, putting out a season pass without telling you what you get for your money…[/list]
 
[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Back 4 Blood is exactly what Left 4 Dead Fans wanted all these years. The gunplay is amazing, the campaign is very good, the swarm mode is fun and it's hard enough. It even evolved in some areas. You now have something to work towards (unlocking things), cards that spice things up a lot, and different runs like in a roguelite.
It has its flaws (a lot of them actually) but you can easily overlook them thanks to how fun the rest of the game is. I would like to have invisible skill-based matchmaking in swarm mode (especially since they already lock you out of MM if you leave early) and an ENDLESS mode like in Left 4 Dead. I also dislike the policy to put out a season pass without announcing what they will offer in it. I appreciate them developing the game further and I hope to see much more content down the line but I wouldn't recommend buying the season pass to anyone as of now.
 
The game is a lot of fun. I definitely recommend it to fans of Left 4 Dead and the likes. I just think the price is a bit too high.

Definite improvement over L4D campaigns.  The card system does a good job making each run unique, giving it solid replayability to a point.  That point being where everyone knows the best card deck to optimize each character... then it gets repetitive.  Characters reveal some of their back story as you play, which is nice. But their snappy one-liners don't compare with L4D and their personalities fall flat as a result.  Swarm (vs) mode is more like survival mode in L4D where one team just survives a single map as long as they can against an onslaught of common ridden controlled by AI and mutations (special infected) controlled by the competing team.  I still prefer L4D approach to vs where one team has to transverse a map and survive an event.  It just feels more fulfilling when you complete the run rather than just struggling until you die; it also gives the infected side a chance for ambushes. The cross-platform community for this game is not toxic (yet).  I attribute that to the fact that you cannot vote off players and you have the option of muting others.  So you can either stick with your team or leave the game.  The player matchmaking seems completely random.  I generally get a mix of skilled players and first-timers; other times I get no one at all. It's a good addition to the L4D universe with some quality campaigns but lack-luster vs mode and a lot of potential for expansion and improvement.

I LOVE horde style shooters and I really enjoy this game, but as it is now I would not recommend it. TRS has brought in patches under the mindset that they want people to work as a team, which is a good thing. However, the implementation has made the game unfairly challenging, compared to its old version of being fairly challenging. 

I can understand their response of 'A Melee build should not be able to hold a door on their own' but nerfing the melee weapons, increasing special HP, AND decreasing stumble chance was unnecessary, it was overkill. It intended effect could have been achieved with just one or two of these.

If they want defined roles in the teams, then a tank is part of that build. If melee is intended to be damage class not a tank class then the cards should reflect that. A tank means taking damage and kiting enemies. So, either the melee needs to be rewarded with health and sustain. Or it is a damage class and is capable of doing high amounts of damage at the cost of health. Or melee is not meant to mean to be either of these things in which case, why have melee weapons and melee cards in the first place?

At this point I can't in good conscience recommend this game in its current state. Go play Vermintide 2.

Between the beta and launch, this game has given me over 100 hours of fun and continues to be fun. With that said, there are some issues that people are understandably upset over—so let us start off there.

[b]Mutations[/b] - The mutations are one of the largest sources of pain this game has currently. First and foremost due to a longstanding bug that causes them to spawn in ridiculous numbers. They have addressed that this is a bigger problem than expected and is taking more time to fix. The second main issue surrounding mutations is that, between the main three categories, the individual types do not stand out much from each other. While they may have different weakpoints or slight color variations, their glance value is all very similar.

[b]RNG & Speedrunning[/b] - For a game based on teamwork, and especially on nightmare, needing to survive sometimes 4+ levels to get a checkpoint, there is a lot of RNG when it comes to the corruption cards. You may only have 2-4 cards of your build when you get a boss, a special horde card, an effect like fog, and every type of zombie has a form of mutation on top of acid ridden. It can feel really bad to only have 1 continue attempt when the game has numerous opportunities to throw away your run. Much to many individual's disappointment, the solution to beating the RNG has shifted greatly towards speed running builds. This is the case even more after melee got nerfed (from very OP to just very strong). People just wanna shoot some zombies and not need to break spawning mechanics in order to progress.

[b]The community[/b] - From the beginning there have been many complaints about trolls and abusive players. With no vote to kick system, and a report system with questionable results, many are upset that it only takes one player to ruin an entire run. With solo progression being a December release, many have been forced to choose between no progression, trolls, or putting the game down. 

While there are some other lesser issues as well, there is a lot of good the game has to offer as well.

[b]Unique Twist[/b] - Zombies shooters and deck builders are far from new, but the combination of the two with some roguelike elements has made this game feel refreshingly new. Being able to bring specialized characters and builds makes me feel like you are actually preparing for the missions and not just thrown in completely unprepared.

[b]Memorable Levels[/b] - For being a zombie shooter, the little bit of back story and the story locations does make you feel like you are running out to the various mission locations. The reuse of some areas enforces how much of a constant threat the ridden are, but done in a way which doesn't feel lazy. When the need for speedrunning isn't as big, getting to enjoy the atmosphere of the levels has been great. There are also many fun references hidden throughout the various safe rooms and levels.

[b]The Community pt 2[/b] - While there are the trolls and whatnot in the game, I have been able to meet many more amazing individuals through both public matchmaking and the various LFG locations. Some of my favorite moments in this game is coming together with a group (randoms or not) and being able to push past a challenging level. If it is beating T-5 when you have no offensive upgrades or finally overcoming 1-4 on Nightmare, the feeling of finally closing that saferoom door with everyone alive has been great.

Much like the cons, there are more pros to the game as well—you could probably write a decent essay on everything. I pre-ordered the ultimate edition and am still happy with my purchase. The game hit a rough spot with its last patch, but it still has its amazing core to build off of. Especially after the December patch, I believe this game will be in an amazing place and more of the rough spots will be leveled out.
